reasons: Datadog averages nginx.net.request_per_s by {host}, but the candidate's avg() has no by-host grouping, so it collapses all hosts into one series.
The template variable $host (prefix host, default *) should add a host matcher such as host=~"$host"; the candidate omits it, so the series set differs.

The nginx.requests definition has no host attribute and observed dataset labels are only [state], so the host grouping cannot be verified or expressed exactly; the candidate silently drops it instead of reporting it.

Quantity is plausibly the same (rate of a monotonic request counter gives requests per second), so the unit is ok, but the aggregation, grouping, and series differ, and translating without the host dimension is not an exact translation.
